findings.title: BuildIndex now allows duplicate concurrent builds for the same index
findings.body: The previous global cacheMu lock around the entire BuildIndex call has been reduced to locking only the final cache write. However, getOrCreateIndex in resource/search.go has no per-key synchronization and checks GetIndex only once before building. Two concurrent callers that miss the same NamespacedResource can both enter BuildIndex. With file-backed indexes, both will call bleve.New on the same directory, which can fail or conflict; one index is then leaked and the cache is overwritten. Add per-key singleflight/locking, or re-check the cache under the lock before building.

findings.title: Data races on shared counters and error variable during parallel index initialization
findings.body: In searchSupport.init, errgroup runs one goroutine per resource. Every goroutine increments the plain int totalBatchesIndexed and assigns the shared outer err variable via `_, _, err = s.build(...)`. These are unsynchronized concurrent writes, so the race detector will flag them and the namespace count metric can be lost. Use atomic operations for the counter and a local error variable inside each goroutine.

findings.title: Search event watcher uses an uncancellable background context and panics on close
findings.body: searchSupport.init starts WatchWriteEvents with `watchctx := context.Background()` instead of the supplied ctx, then launches a goroutine that does `v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v)` in an infinite loop. This goroutine cannot be stopped by server.Stop/s.cancel. When the backend closes the events channel during shutdown, the receive returns a nil *WrittenEvent and handleEvent dereferences evt.Type, panicking and crashing the process. Because Init is now eager, this watcher is created during NewResourceServer for every process rather than only after a request.

findings.title: Starting search index build before watchers creates a write-event gap during startup
findings.body: Init now runs s.search.init to completion before s.initWatcher is called. The SQL backend's WatchWriteEvents snapshots the latest resource versions when it is called and only emits later events. Because the initial index build can take a long time and runs before either the search or server watcher starts, any writes committed during the build are not indexed and are not broadcast to Watch clients, leaving both stale until a subsequent write. The last RV returned by the build is discarded, and there is no backfill from that point.

findings.title: Postgres storage server integration test is newly skipped without a fix
findings.body: The test is now explicitly skipped for Postgres with a TODO, and the diff does not add equivalent coverage. Since the storage server is the target affected by eager initialization and watcher ordering changes, losing this integration test removes protection against regressions on Postgres.
